This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 26.04.2022 passed by Ist MACT, Sardarpur, district Dhar in Claim Case No.24/2020 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Madanlal, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,49,711/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.3,59,964/-
 (i.e. Rs.5000 - 1/3 PE=3333 x 12 x 9 (m))
 Consortium -Rs.1,32,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 Medical Bills -Rs.24,747/-
 ----------------------
 TOTAL Rs.5,49,711/-
3.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.5000/- per month.
Even if there was no proof of actual income, the same ought to have been assessed on the basis of the minimum wages for an unskilled labour for the relevant period.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any sum under the head of future prospects.
Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

The accident was occurred on 13.11.2019, therefore, considering the minimum wages of an unskilled labour for the relevant period,
the income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.7,950 per month.

As per the evidence, the deceased was sixty years of age at the time of accident, therefore, the claimants are entitled for 10% future Smt. Bhagwatibai vs Sonik on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16466070/
2 prospects.

sentences.text:
Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal deserves to be modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.6,29,640/-
 (i.e. Rs.7,950 10% F.P - 1/3 PE x 12 x 9 (m))
 Consortium -Rs.1,32,000/-
 Medical Bills -Rs.24,747/-
 Other heads -Rs.43,000/-
 -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.8,29,387/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,29,387/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.5,49,711/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,79,676/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,79,676/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
